answer: For a vote on replacing ferrous lantern fittings in a grove, give trusted residents fixed budgets of signed vote credits. Validators accept transfers only if they consume existing unspent credits; splitting a credit preserves its total weight. Each ballot spends credits once across all keys. An attacker creating aliases must obtain more of the same finite endorsement budget, displacing other uses rather than minting influence. Residents can collude or sell their budgets, so initial allocation remains a trust assumption.
